references.shows: The Met’s ivory cornetto in A has a curved octagonal body, gilt ferrule and small cup mouthpiece.
A neutral photo of a similar ivory cornett shows six front fingerholes along the wider half of the curve.

silhouette: A slender, gently curved body widens gradually toward the open end.
features: A single slim curved body widens gradually toward a small open foot.
Six fingerholes follow the wider half of the front face.
The small cup mouthpiece seats in the narrow end above a short gilt ferrule.
iconFeatures: A gently curved single body tapering toward the mouthpiece in playing position.
avoid: Contours that obscure the characteristic tubing path
notes: The ivory Met specimen guides the proportions and gilt ferrule. The playing view exposes the six front holes while the thumbhole sits on the back.

geometry.view: Side view in the plane of the curve
geometry.proportions: A slender, gently curved body widens gradually toward the open end.
geometry.partLayout: Place six holes along the wider half of the visible face. Seat the cup mouthpiece in the narrow end. The foot remains close in width to the adjoining body.

documentedDimensions.value: 57.2 cm long and about 7 cm across the widest curve.
